findings.title: Main checkpoint continuation replaces the journal identity before completed-tool replay

evidence.detail: Matching checkpoint restores mainAgentState and sets resumeInterruptedTurn=true.
Only pinnedRunId skips startAgentRun; normal checkpoint continuation mints and assigns a new runId at 1973.
Production startAgentRun returns a fresh local-run UUID.

Wiring test manually supplies the old runId to the reader instead of executing checkpoint continuation.

findings.trigger: A process dies after a programmatic tool_result was committed but before the next checkpoint; the TUI reloads the older checkpoint and resends its matching prompt.
findings.consequence: Observed DI: replay lookup runs under a new ID while the original completed result remains present. Inference: re-derived non-idempotent programmatic calls can execute again because the old result is unreachable to this guard.
findings.suggestedFix: Pin the interrupted main run's durable identity, with an explicit fresh-turn versus resume contract; preserve/reconstruct replay position against that journal rather than reminting it.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Seed an original journal and older main checkpoint; resume through the real SDK/loop with a unique production-style startAgentRun; assert the completed effect's counter stays one, the old stream remains authoritative, and a subsequent new user turn gets a fresh identity.

findings.title: Model-driven tool dispatch lacks P2 journal boundaries and uncertain-effect reconciliation

evidence.detail: Model-native calls enter executeToolCall directly; custom/MCP calls use executeCustomToolCall at 731.
tool_call/tool_result journal boundaries and completed-result replay live in executeSingleToolCall's programmatic path.
Shared executor only force-flushes an optional writer; it does not append tool boundary events.
Production SDK dispatch calls handleToolCall without P2 journal writer/reader; its signature at 2180–2265 has none.
Optional Memory V2 observation runs after handled output; it is not the P2 replay contract.
MCP dispatch calls the external tool and returns output directly.
No completed match means live re-execution; no ambiguous-effect receipt is returned.
The kill-9-labelled fixture appends B's intent without executing B pre-crash.

findings.trigger: A model-selected shell/custom/MCP operation applies, then the process dies before the next recoverable transcript/result; or a programmatic effect applies between its intent and result records.
findings.consequence: Observed DI: model read_files runs and enters history while the P2 journal has only llm_request/llm_response/step_boundary. Static production trace confirms no SDK compensation for these missing boundaries. Inference: restart cannot distinguish 'not applied' from 'applied but unacknowledged' and may repeat non-idempotent effects.
findings.suggestedFix: Put effect intent/result recording at a shared native/custom/MCP dispatch boundary. Persist a stable operation identity and classify uncertain results explicitly; reconcile supported external effects or require a concrete user decision before repeating them. Keep filesystem broker recovery separate and reuse its receipts where applicable.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use a DI counter and a real temporary journal; kill a helper after the counter increments but before its result receipt. Restart the actual dispatcher and assert no blind repeat: it must reconcile, report an unknown outcome, or request the required decision. Include native model tools, programmatic tools, custom tools and MCP.
findings.scope: P2 run-journal/replay coverage. This finding does not claim filesystem broker receipts, process-job records, or optional Memory V2 traces are absent.

findings.title: Parent turn cleanup closes the shared journal while detached children are still running

evidence.detail: The TUI closes the journal at the parent run promise-chain end.
Headless command also closes the journal when its parent run returns.
Detached child receives the same journal writer/reader references.
Own-journal re-drive is deliberately launched detached with inherited params.
After close, append silently returns.
Close contract explicitly acknowledges that an outliving child stops journaling.

findings.trigger: A background agent, including a resumed child, outlives the successful/cancelled parent turn whose CLI opened its journal.
findings.consequence: Its later requests, results, and terminal tail are dropped. Inference: a later process restart may reconstruct stale child history, leave a respawn marker unsettled, or lose the result; avoiding closed-database exceptions does not preserve child durability.
findings.suggestedFix: Give journals session/process ownership with child-aware reference counting, or give each detached child an independently owned connection. Persist settlement to the current durable parent/session record rather than only mutating a captured old AgentState.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Hold a child on a DI gate, let the parent return and perform real CLI cleanup, release the child, reopen the disk journal, and assert the child's final result/tail and parent settlement exist. Repeat with cooperative parent cancellation.

findings.title: ACP prompts and session/load do not restore an executable conversation

evidence.detail: Each prompt calls client.run without previousRun, onCheckpoint or P2 journal handles; returned RunState is discarded.
SDK conversation continuation requires passing previousRun.
Durable ACP store contains receipt, gate, capability and workspace-revision maps, not the transcript/main AgentState.
Chat-history replay requires optional historyLoader, which runServe does not wire.
Derived loader ignores restoreFromJournal=false.
Resume/replay advertisement derives from journalAvailable.
hasJournal checks only whether journalDir was configured.

findings.trigger: Send a follow-up in one ACP session, or load its ID after a serve restart, including an ID with no journal.
findings.consequence: Observed DI: the second prompt carries no prior RunState; an absent session loads successfully with {} while journal availability is advertised. The model's prior conversation and executable workflow state do not continue even though receipt/gate projections can reload.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a per-session durable RunState/transcript owner; route previousRun and checkpoint/journal handles through it and provide the actual history loader. Advertise executable resume only when this path is available, and return typed missing/corrupt-session outcomes.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Run two DI prompts where the second depends on a first-turn constraint, then restart the service over a temp store and load the ID. Assert the core sees that constraint, history is replayed, checkpoints use the same session, and invented/missing IDs fail distinctly.

findings.title: ACP reattachment loses running-turn cancellation ownership and bypasses the prompt guard

evidence.detail: Every socket creates a fresh ACP agent with its own private session map.
Run AbortControllers are stored in that per-connection map.
Loading on a fresh connection creates a record with a null controller; it only preserves an existing same-connection controller.
The concurrent-prompt guard checks that connection-local controller.
Detach destroys the owned transport and keeps the session ID for load on a new connection.
Cancel addresses only the current connection's session record.
Socket detach test waits until the prompt completed; it does not exercise a live reattachment.

findings.trigger: Detach/reconnect or connect another authorized client and load an ID while the original long tool/model turn remains live.
findings.consequence: Observed DI with two production-style agents sharing one store: cancellation on the loaded session does not abort the original run, and a second prompt is admitted before the first settles. Inference: two runs can mutate the same served workspace with no session-level guard or usable control over the first.
findings.suggestedFix: Own running turns in a service-wide session registry and attach connection sinks/controllers to that owner. Define detach and disconnect semantics explicitly; a new client must observe/join/cancel the same turn and preserve the per-session prompt exclusion.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Hold a first run on a gate; disconnect and reconnect through the actual socket backend; load its ID and attempt cancel/another prompt. Assert cancel reaches the original controller and a new prompt is rejected until settlement or explicitly queued.
findings.assuranceLimit: The DI probe uses two connection-level agents; no real socket disconnect was executed. Installed ACP 1.5 legacy adapter passes params to implementation.prompt without its connection request signal; vendor code is excluded from the structural receipt.

findings.title: A killed socket service leaves an anonymous lock that blocks restart indefinitely

evidence.detail: Socket lock is exclusively created but receives no PID/token/owner record.
Any existing lock is refused before stale-socket cleanup.
Lock removal is only graceful cleanup or bind/setup error handling.
Cleanup coverage closes gracefully; it does not kill a lock owner.

findings.trigger: The serve process is SIGKILLed or crashes after acquiring socketPath.lock; the user restarts serve at the same socket path.
findings.consequence: Observed DI: the production startup path refuses an otherwise safe directory containing that anonymous stale lock. An actual process kill cannot execute releaseLock, so automatic restart remains blocked until manual cleanup.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a crash-recoverable, ownership-verified lock with a recorded owner and safe stale-owner reconciliation, reusing proven store lock patterns. Surface recoverable stale-lock versus live-owner conflict distinctly.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Launch a temp socket service, wait for ownership, SIGKILL the helper, restart at the identical path and verify successful bind without deleting another live owner's lock. Also cover stale socket/non-socket refusal and permission failure.

findings.title: Live child path leases expire because production spawns never heartbeat them

evidence.detail: Default lease TTL is thirty minutes.
The next acquisition sweeps expired runtime leases without checking child liveness.
Real batch spawn acquires a lease and only releases it in settle/rollback paths.
Inline spawn uses the same acquire/release pattern.
Extension helper exists; repository consumer search found only tests calling it.
Productive subagent durations are unbounded by default.

findings.trigger: A writable child runs past the thirty-minute TTL and another child requests an overlapping path.
findings.consequence: Observed shortened-TTL DI: overlap is admitted while the original durable lease still says active. The advertised exclusive child scope ceases to exclude a still-running writer. Separate processes also have independent path maps; the exported disk-backed WorkspaceLeaseService is not wired into spawns.
findings.suggestedFix: Tie lease renewal/release to actual child supervision and cancellation; route participating processes through one durable lease authority if cross-process ownership is promised. Preserve fencing/generation checks so an expired owner cannot resume writing after a replacement acquires.
findings.acceptanceProbe: With an injected clock, keep one writable child live across multiple TTLs, request overlap, and assert refusal until terminal settlement. Exercise abrupt owner death, lost renewal, cancellation and a stale owner's attempted renewal.

findings.consequence: No advisory state/revision update or structured illegal-transition result is recorded through this branch. This is an unwired telemetry/resumability feature; it does not establish a defect in the authoritative generator gate (owned by pair03).
findings.suggestedFix: Expose the safe helper under the member name the serialized consumer expects and give the injected control-plane contract one typed/shared definition.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Drive the real runProgrammaticStep-to-shipped-base2 path without manually adding the helper; assert workflowStates revision advances and an illegal transition persists a structured error while authoritative gate behavior remains unchanged.

findings.title: Concurrent snapshot producers can orphan a snapshot they report as created

evidence.detail: Successful-turn snapshot runs fire-and-forget before the queue is released.
Each producer separately reads the private ref's current parent.
Publication uses unconditional update-ref without an expected old SHA.
Guard excludes bisection but does not serialize concurrent snapshot producers.
Concurrency coverage concerns bisection ownership, not two snapshot publications.

findings.trigger: Two CLI processes, or a slow prior-turn snapshot and another producer, capture distinct trees and read the same private-ref tip before publishing.
findings.consequence: Observed DI: both return created but publish sibling commits with the same parent through unconditional update-ref. Inference: only the last remains in the listed chain; one successful recovery point can disappear, and a slow end-turn capture can contain later mutations.
findings.suggestedFix: Serialize capture and publication per repository and compare-and-swap the expected ref tip. Define a bounded turn/shell snapshot barrier; cancel or mark late captures accurately instead of letting them publish a later tree as an earlier boundary.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use two temp-repo producers with barriers at parent read/publication; assert both successful snapshots remain in one chain or one fails/retries explicitly. Queue a fast mutating next turn behind a slow capture and verify turn attribution.

findings.title: JSON replay emits empty assistant text for the runtime's response record shape

evidence.detail: Runtime llm_response stores {messageId, fullResponse}.
JSON mapper reads only payload.text or payload.message, falling back to empty text.
The mapper is the actual --json replay/export consumer.

findings.trigger: Run openbuff replay <id> --json against an ordinary journalled plain assistant response produced by the runtime.
findings.consequence: Observed DI with the production payload shape: replay exits zero and emits {type:'text',text:''}; the retained assistant answer disappears from the machine-readable replay/evaluation fixture.
findings.suggestedFix: Define and share a versioned journal response schema that explicitly stores model-visible text; make replay consume it and handle existing fullResponse rows deliberately without re-executing tools.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Journal a plain response through the real loop, replay --json, and assert the original visible text and ordering survive. Include legacy rows, tool-containing responses and empty/error records.

domainAssessment.security: Considered socket directory ownership/permissions, token gates, ACP session ID containment, restored wire redaction/schema checks, snapshot untracked collisions and cooperative ownership. Existing auth/path/redaction controls are strengths. No new injection/auth bypass claim is made; path leases are cooperative rather than OS isolation. Live external effects and private state were not accessed.
domainAssessment.correctness: Observed main resume ID replacement, model-tool P2 journal asymmetry, ACP state loss/false missing-session load, connection-local controller loss, lease expiry, snapshot publication race and replay response-field mismatch. Background own-journal relaunch is a real partial feature; foreground re-drive is a logging seam.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Traced checkpoint capture/queue/clear, parent journal close versus detached children, ACP merge/queues/controllers, LocalHarnessStore CAS, task-memory file lock, workflow state writes and Git private-ref update. Atomic rename and locked merges are useful; lifetime/ownership boundaries remain incomplete.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Normal CLI journal open failures warn and continue; reader/restore failures degrade differently. ACP queued writes swallow errors and in-place rewrites have no hard-crash acknowledgement/drain boundary. Socket stale locks block restart. V1 memory locks deliberately refuse even orphaned residue, preserving exclusion but leaving an indefinite save outage without a recovery surface. No generalized uncertain external-effect outcome is exposed.
domainAssessment.performance: Inspected prepared statements, indexed bounded tails, retention caps, dashboard bounded listings/details, batched journal/stdio paths, lease sweeps and ACP bounded receipts. Dashboard getRunEvents calls full events() before slicing; optional response bounds do not establish bounded hydration. ACP map/queue lifetime and in-place full rewrite lack measured workload assurance. No benchmark, latency, CPU or memory magnitude is claimed.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: SDK declares @agentclientprotocol/sdk ^1.5.0 and Zod, and the journal uses Bun's built-in SQLite with structural injection. Installed ACP 1.5 legacy adapter was inspected only to resolve connection-signal behavior; it is not in the pinned structural receipt. Floating dependency/API compatibility and Node/Windows packaging were not executed; no vulnerability assertion is invented.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: All 38 selected ranges, including selected checkpoint/SQLite/ACP restoration tests, were read. Existing tests cover actual disk round-trips, graceful reopen, temp Git materialization, controlled cancellation, same-process path leases and seeded background loop integration. The kill-9-labelled effect fixture does not kill/apply its incomplete effect. Eight isolated DI probes passed (24 assertions); these verify wiring/behavior but not real provider, process-kill or live transport restart recovery.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Direct member/schema drift: transitionBase2GateSafe versus injected transitionBase2Gate; llm_response.fullResponse versus replay.text/message. ACP loadSession can accept an absent session while resume/replay advertisement depends only on configured journalDir. Remote RunState has no sessionState; durable projections are not an executable session contract. Lanes advertise unsupported=false and return capability_disabled consistently.

coverageLimits: Inspection receipt covers 73 current inventory files via bounded exact ranges, not a full-line audit of every listed file. All 38 picker-selected ranges are covered; adjacent reads are enumerated. Native retrieval/audit tools are unavailable in this Codex session; root will validate the native structural receipt through exported repository code.

Existing repository suites were inspected, not rerun. Only the 8-case isolated DI audit file was executed (Bun 1.3.14, 24 assertions, 0 failures). Fake providers throw/return controlled values; Git runner is injected. No real root-repo Git changes, credentials/private local state, external API, or live-provider run was used.

No actual SIGKILL/restart of the CLI/service, ACP socket detach while a provider call is live, Node public package invocation, Windows transport, or daemon boot was exercised. The socket-lock probe supplies the exact anonymous residue shape instead of killing a real listener.

Installed node_modules/@agentclientprotocol/sdk/dist/acp.js was read at 995–1015 and 1164–1178 to confirm the legacy adapter passes params without its request signal. This non-inventory dependency is excluded from structuralReceipt.files.

Provider routing and generator terminal-state authority are owned by pairs02/03; journal/lease/serialization consequences are assessed here only. Memory quality/compaction/V2 retention belongs to pair04; mutation exact-byte authority to pair06; process/OS containment to pair09; broad task/control-plane completeness to pair12.

Default TUI/headless run journaling is separate from optional SDK journal injection. Foreground resume adapters report attempts, not actual resumed child execution. The separate exported WorkspaceLeaseService is real for explicit SDK callers but unwired into default spawns.

Snapshot materialization deliberately retains target-absent tracked paths and excludes untracked files; it is not a full deletion-aware rollback. Retention's repo-global refs/replace mutation is disclosed. Hard-kill bisection restoration was not verified.

ACP JSONL has real receipt/gate reload and fill-only live merge, but its queue is best-effort, full rewrites truncate in place, and no shutdown acknowledgement/drain is exposed. Its main-lane revision map is not rehydrated by the restore receipt loop. These are capability limits beyond the ranked session/control defects.

Dashboard default CLI wires only the run-journal source; receipt/gate seams remain empty/null unless explicitly supplied. An absent reader is checked at startup and not automatically opened after another process creates the journal. Pagination/hydration at realistic retained-history size is unmeasured.

Plan/task artifact persistence is traced through get_task and STATE.json, not promoted into durable workflow execution. Ordinary writePlanState increments/replaces state without a cross-process CAS; pair12 owns broader task-source consistency.

V1 memory persistence correctly fails closed on an orphaned exclusive-create lock; its test deliberately requires that result. The resulting indefinite save outage requires explicit safe recovery design rather than blindly deleting lock residue.

probeRuns.limits: Real loop/helpers and in-memory SQLite; two connection-level agents/fake client, simulated stale lock, shortened lease TTL, fake Git. No live provider/socket restart/actual kill.
